Decision Log Lab

A year of the Reef team: 30 architecture decisions, 3 people leave, 3 join, and 24 times someone asks "why is it like this?". Choose where the reasons live, what a record says, and how changed decisions are kept, then see how many questions get an answer and how many decisions get undone by accident.

One year, 24 "why?" questions. Goal: 0 accidental reversals and at most 40 hours spent on writing records, re-debating and incidents together.

Lesson 068: architecture decision records

    What this shows

    Reasons leave with people

    Chat scrolls away and people move on. A decision whose reason is gone gets argued again, or quietly undone.

    The "why" is the point

    A record that says only what was chosen invites the same debate. Context and consequences (what we gave up) are what end it.

    Never edit history

    When a decision changes, write a new record and mark the old one superseded. The path from old to new is often the answer to the next question.

    This lab is a model, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 068's numbers: 30 decisions in a year, 24 "why?" questions, 3 people leave (months 3, 6, 9) and 3 join. Reasons are found for 8 questions when they live in heads and chat, 12 in design docs that get rewritten, 12 in records that say only what was chosen, 20 in full records edited in place (the 4 about changed decisions lose their history), and 24 with superseding records. A question without an answer costs a 6-hour re-debate; 1 in 4 of them ends with the decision undone, causing an incident of 30 hours. A record costs 0.5 hours to write with the decision only, 1 hour with context and consequences.
